schema_review.rationale: The reusable Server migration framework registers actual PowerContext 1.3.0 through s1300 -> s1400 -> s1401 -> s1402 and actual 1.4.0 through the separate immutable r1400 -> s1400 -> s1401 -> s1402 source bridge. Original 1.3 resources and checksums remain byte-identical. Real 1.4.0 SQLite, embedded seekDB and OceanBase structures were captured from the official wheel in all twelve vector/Code configurations; provenance and exact source layouts are packaged with the bridge. The 1.4 bridge preserves current Candidate, Artifact and task data, adds the missing Topic budget/block structure, revokes old lease fences and joins the existing archive/portable-storage path. Empty retained tables align the final schema without inventing 1.3 Candidate history. Source histories retain their identity through subsequent upgrades and recovery; shared head names never authorize adopting unknown layouts. Vector profiles remain bound to historical model, profile ID, dimension, unit normalization and L2 distance, with no provider calls during maintenance. Complete schema, domain, projection, profile and retained-history checks precede startup and partial maintenance. Local SQLite and embedded seekDB startup reject an observable active maintenance lock through a read-only probe. SQLite runtime admission validates the default adjacent journal, rejecting unfinished full or partial maintenance, changed recorded revision checksums and missing required retained tables. Absent journals do not invent retention obligations; custom evidence directories require explicit operator verification and remote coordinator locks remain subject to deployment orchestration. Native read-only readiness uses a consistent snapshot and does not acquire Atomic Memory head locks; normal business transaction isolation is unchanged. Offline projection repairs retain the original locked state comparison and write-side CAS protection. Target locks, backup choices, original recovery evidence and explicit remote acknowledgments remain enforced. The installed-artifact catalog retains twelve 1.3.0 source/backend/vector/Code combinations. Embedded seekDB uses pylibseekdb 1.4.0.post2 or newer with the recovered-transaction lock fix. Main and publication require all twelve configurations, including embedded seekDB full-server-code and full-server-vector-code. No configuration is waived; incomplete, failed or skipped evidence rejects acceptance. The seekdb-code diagnostic selection cannot authorize publication. The registered 1.4.0 bridge remains implemented but is outside the CI upgrade acceptance matrix; passing this gate does not certify that path. The gate preserves source-specific Processing counters and isolates OceanBase source databases. Any failed, skipped or missing automatic case rejects publication. The policy remains upgrade-required until the exact target artifact passes the required automatic matrix and the reviewed support declaration is updated. Captured source structure, local tests and checkpoint replay are distinct from installed-release acceptance, native interruption/observer recovery and backup restoration. The Candidate generation prototype observes actual SQLite/seekDB/OceanBase migration checkpoints outside the production bundle; it does not replace frozen registrations or weaken recovery checks. Existing target schema and data formats, including batched persistence interfaces, remain governed by the shared registered path. The synchronized master adds blank-text validation at Source creation and managed worker logging. It changes neither registered table layout nor migration data encodings; existing stored Source values are not rewritten. The source bridges and frozen history remain unchanged. Compatibility commands identify Server-owned storage before opening a writable legacy profile and delegate source admission to the shared framework, including actual 1.4.0 and rejection of unknown layouts. Partial Processing and Atomic Memory projection maintenance verify the original recorded revision checksums; native admission also validates typed journal identity and its completed position against the database revision. Persisted vector profiles reject unsupported partial maintenance before plans, backups or operation evidence, including when the supplied configuration omits embeddings. These are admission-only changes; frozen migration resources, registered layouts, historical checksums and data transformations remain unchanged. PowerContext 1.4.1 assigns release-based presentation names v1_4_1_001 through v1_4_1_003 to the existing shared upgrade steps; the 1.3.0 and 1.4.0 source baselines remain independently registered. Existing revision IDs, bundle and revision checksums, accepted plan identities and journal schemas are unchanged. New Server revisions use software-version-plus-sequence names directly; software releases without storage changes may reuse the same database revision. Naming does not grant acceptance or replace source registration. Full Server status, plan, apply and verify reject unfinished Processing configuration and Atomic Memory projection journals through the same typed admission check used by partial maintenance and SQLite startup. The owning domain runner can still resume its own journal. This only changes admission; frozen revisions, journal formats, database layouts and data transformations remain unchanged. Revision v1_4_1_004 registers the pc_access_owner_recovery outbox on the shared Server chain for both installed-release sources and all registered vector/Code profiles. It creates an empty table through explicit maintenance for existing managed databases and through the registered bootstrap for fresh databases. Earlier revision resources, fingerprints, checksums and existing domain row encodings remain unchanged. External relationship writers use version-1 Artifact and Candidate intents committed with domain data; replay retains the original deployment, principal, resource or target, and idempotency identity. Stable operation and audit event identities prevent lost acknowledgements from duplicating ownership or audit. Conflicting intents are rejected and unknown historical ownership is not inferred. Unregistered outbox layouts are not adopted merely from a table name. This registration does not establish installed-release or external-Provider upgrade acceptance. The policy remains upgrade-required with the full automatic matrix and publication restrictions described above. Database selection now defaults to powercontext for seekDB and for OceanBase URLs without a database, while explicit database names remain authoritative. An implicit seekDB selection is rejected before initialization when the legacy test database contains pc_ tables; operators can explicitly select database=test to retain those records, and no database is moved or deleted automatically. Bootstrap reuses an accessible selected database without CREATE privilege and creates only a confirmed missing database, with idempotent creation and explicit permission errors. Read-only maintenance on an initialized MySQL-compatible engine requires the selected database and never provisions it; an absent or empty seekDB instance remains a no-engine initial plan. MySQL initialization creates only missing requested tables and indexes, and sorts only those requested tables; existing registered tables are preserved. Code graph connections use the selected database, retain historical graph identities for test, and distinguish other database identities. Server identity initialization avoids redundant MySQL DDL on an existing table. Frozen migration resources, revision identifiers and checksums, registered table definitions, journal formats, and existing row encodings are unchanged. These runtime selection and admission changes do not establish an accepted upgrade path; the policy remains upgrade-required and the installed-release acceptance gate still applies. MySQL recovery rejects different registered table sets before normalization. Backend-default normalization copies only the column and index maps it changes and compares each table without cloning whole inventories. Admitted layouts, registered transitions, recovery checks, schema equality and caller-owned inventories remain preserved. SeekDB status and verify distinguish a missing configured database from an uninitialized engine and denied access. Read-only plan can represent a missing selected database as an uninitialized target without creating it; apply provisions that selected database only after the operator accepts its bound plan, then rechecks the target under the maintenance lock. Installed-release seekDB acceptance explicitly retains the historical test database and separately verifies that omitted selection is refused. Registered schema resources, revision checksums, row encodings and write-side provisioning remain unchanged. Server startup can apply an uninitialized plan to provision a missing selected seekDB database; plan, status and verify still never provision it. OceanBase 4.6 SHOW CREATE TABLE can reflect FTS_INDEX_TYPE=MATCH or PHRASE_MATCH on FULLTEXT indexes. Reflection accepts these known types without changing the logical inventory; unknown values remain rejected and indexed columns, parser identity and token-size properties remain significant. PHRASE_MATCH additionally supports phrase matching; the registered layouts require term matching and do not declare a phrase-only contract. Frozen migration resources, checksums, recovery evidence and persisted layouts remain unchanged. Native 4.6.3.1 DDL was captured from a real installed 1.3.0 database; replay of this fixture does not establish complete native upgrade acceptance. The CI database image and master full automatic upgrade matrix remain unchanged. Revision v1_4_1_005 adds nullable Atomic Memory description projection metadata after the registered owner-recovery revision, through explicit SQLite and MySQL schema transitions for both source chains and all vector/Code profiles. Earlier revision resources, fingerprints and checksums remain unchanged. The additive change neither rewrites authoritative Artifact history nor generates summaries or scans stored bodies. Existing managed databases require explicit migration; existing descriptions remain null until a new write or explicit projection repair copies authoritative metadata. Intermediate projection validation uses only columns available at that revision and still rejects inconsistent existing fields. Unmanaged SDK initialization retains its nullable-column compatibility path. The installed-release acceptance matrix and publication restrictions remain required; local regression checks do not establish native upgrade acceptance. Artifact plugin storage extends the shared Server chain from v1_4_1_006 to v1_5_0_001 with registration columns, family declarations, search state and projections, index coverage and changes, and vector-space/index registrations. SQLite also registers portable vectors and FTS auxiliary structures. Native registration columns are added in one ALTER with a matching recovery checkpoint; final column definitions and constraints are unchanged. Native vector tables are created online from registered spaces and are admitted to later maintenance inventories only after exact layout validation. Historical migration resources, retained objects, and existing data are preserved. This review does not expand the supported upgrade matrix or certify installed-release acceptance. Source write plugin registrations use the additive v1_4_1_006 revision after v1_4_1_005 on both source chains. It creates only pc_source_write_plugins; all earlier master revision scripts, schema resources and checksums remain unchanged. Code generation publication now records a caller-assigned generation identifier in a private binding-local publication.json sidecar before graph writes and records the final directory before rename. Missing sidecars retain the legacy empty-record interpretation; existing manifests, graph descriptors and generation directories keep their original read paths. Recovery reclaims only recorded, unretained identifiers, and seekDB deletion is scoped through the owning binding; live generation directories and reader leases remain protected. SQLite graph rows remain inside their generation directory. No registered database table, migration resource, revision checksum or existing row encoding changes. Legacy generations without publication records are not retrospectively assigned new identities or claimed to be reclaimable after their directories disappear. The sidecar recovery checks do not establish live seekDB/OceanBase or installed-release upgrade acceptance; the full automatic matrix and upgrade-required publication restrictions remain in force.
